The fraction simplifies to $2 + 2\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{3} - \sqrt{6}$, which can be written as $2(1+\sqrt{2}) - (\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{6})$. So $A=2$, $B=2$, $C=3$, $D=6$, and $A+B+C+D = 13$. Solution 3 gets this right.

Solution 1 makes an algebra error when it regroups the terms, and its final answer of 8 is wrong. Solution 2 drops the $\sqrt{6}$ term by writing $-\sqrt{3}(1+\sqrt{2})$ as $-\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{6}$ with $D=0$, which is incorrect.
